description: Signal catalog for FRU-level diagnosis. required signals are needed for initial localization; enhancing signals improve confidence; active_test signals require user or repair-station action.

signal_levels.required: Minimum evidence for initial FRU-level localization.
signal_levels.enhancing: Additional evidence that improves confidence or separates adjacent FRUs.
signal_levels.active_test: Interactive or offline test used when passive OS inventory is insufficient.

required.description: Whether the system reports external AC power.
Power-source, charging, ACPI, or Kernel-Power errors.

enhancing.description: Estimated charging behavior when AC is connected.
Detected adapter wattage, if supported by firmware or active tester.

active_test.description: Check whether the adapter is detected and provides expected wattage.

replacement_limitations: Bad wall outlet, power strip, USB-C cable, or dock can mimic adapter failure.
Motherboard charging IC, DC-in path, or Type-C power-delivery fault can remain after replacing the adapter.

enhancing.description: Full-charge capacity divided by design capacity.
Battery, ACPI, or Kernel-Power related events.

replacement_limitations: Charging circuit, EC firmware, BIOS battery calibration, or adapter fault may persist after battery replacement.
Operating-system power policy or driver fault can cause false battery symptoms.

required.description: Disk, Ntfs, storahci, stornvme, or bad-block events.

enhancing.description: Free-space ratio used to separate capacity issues from drive faults.

active_test.description: Controlled read/write latency and error test.

replacement_limitations: M.2 slot, PCIe lane, motherboard, firmware, filesystem corruption, or OS image damage may remain after replacing the SSD.
Data loss is not repaired by hardware replacement unless backups or recovery are available.

required.description: BugCheck, WHEA, memory-management, or memory-diagnostic events.

active_test.description: Windows Memory Diagnostic or MemTest-style offline result.

replacement_limitations: Memory slot, CPU memory controller, BIOS timing, or motherboard fault can remain after replacing the RAM module.
Driver bugs can produce memory-like crashes without RAM failure.

required.description: WLAN, Netwtw, Bluetooth, link-flap, or adapter-reset events.

replacement_limitations: Router, AP, ISP, antenna cable, driver, OS network stack, or motherboard M.2 E-key slot may remain faulty after WLAN replacement.

required.description: Thermal, throttling, fan, or unexpected power events.

enhancing.description: CPU load for interpreting thermal behavior.

replacement_limitations: Dust blockage, incorrect thermal paste, heatsink damage, EC fan curve, BIOS, or motherboard fan driver fault may persist after fan replacement.

active_test.description: Temperature rise and recovery curve under controlled load.

replacement_limitations: High ambient temperature, blocked vents, poor assembly, thermal paste, chassis deformation, or fan control problems may remain after heatsink replacement.

required.description: WHEA, ACPI, PCIe, firmware, or multi-bus platform events.
Number of PnP devices reporting problems.

enhancing.description: Problem devices with class and error code.

replacement_limitations: Firmware, BIOS settings, OS image, drivers, external peripherals, liquid corrosion beyond the board, or multiple simultaneous module faults may remain after motherboard replacement.

required.description: Display panel or monitor PnP problem code. Zero means no device-manager problem.
Display, graphics, dxgkrnl, nvlddmkm, or igfx events.

enhancing.description: Monitor status, if exposed by Windows.

active_test.description: External display works while internal panel fails.
Panel, backlight, color, and pixel test.

replacement_limitations: GPU, motherboard, eDP cable, driver, OS display stack, or BIOS graphics setting can remain faulty after panel replacement.

required.description: Camera PnP problem code. Zero means no device-manager problem.

replacement_limitations: Privacy setting, camera permission, driver, cable, USB internal bus, or motherboard fault may remain after camera replacement.

required.description: Keyboard, HID, or I2C HID events.

replacement_limitations: Keyboard connector, embedded controller, BIOS setting, filter driver, or OS input stack may remain faulty after keyboard replacement.

required.description: Touchpad or I2C HID device presence.
Touchpad, HID, or I2C HID events.

enhancing.description: Touchpad PnP problem code. Zero means no device-manager problem.

active_test.description: Pointer movement, click, and gesture test.

replacement_limitations: I2C controller, keyboard deck cable, BIOS setting, driver, or OS input setting can remain faulty after touchpad replacement.
Muted output, wrong output device, audio driver, audio codec, amplifier path, motherboard, or OS audio service can remain faulty after speaker replacement.

required.description: Platform events that may affect status LEDs.

replacement_limitations: BIOS/EC firmware, LED cable, motherboard control circuit, or software lighting utility can remain faulty after LED board replacement.

required.description: USB, UcmUcsi, Type-C, audio jack, LAN, or port events.

enhancing.description: LAN adapter status if the port is on the I/O path.
Audio jack or audio subsystem status.

replacement_limitations: Motherboard-side USB/PCIe controller, cable, driver, OS stack, external device, or dock can remain faulty after I/O board replacement.

cross_cutting_non_fru_faults.effect: Module replacement may not change the symptom.

examples: Secure Boot or device disable setting
cross_cutting_non_fru_faults.effect: The hardware module can be healthy but disabled or mismanaged.
Replacing only the endpoint module may not repair the path.
Replacing SSD, Wi-Fi, panel, keyboard, touchpad, or adapter may not solve motherboard-side faults.
The laptop module may be normal while the environment causes the symptom.

examples: fall damage affecting panel and cable
cross_cutting_non_fru_faults.effect: Replacing one module can leave another failed module in the chain.
